_note: Nacha return codes. category drives the triage action; nacha_rate says which Nacha return-rate limit the code counts toward.

R01.name: Insufficient Funds
R01.note: May be re-presented up to 2 times within 180 days of the original settlement date.

R02.name: Account Closed
R02.note: The customer's bank account was closed. They must link a new account.

R03.name: No Account / Unable to Locate Account
R03.note: The account number doesn't match a real account. Often a typo; sometimes a fake account.

R04.name: Invalid Account Number Structure
R04.note: The account number fails format checks. The customer must re-enter bank details.

R05.name: Unauthorized Debit to Consumer Account Using Corporate SEC Code
R05.note: Counts toward the 0.5% unauthorized return rate limit.

R07.name: Authorization Revoked by Customer
R07.note: The customer revoked permission. Never debit again without new authorization. Counts toward the 0.5% unauthorized limit.

R08.name: Payment Stopped
R08.note: The customer placed a stop payment. Do not re-present.

R09.name: Uncollected Funds
R09.note: Treated like R01: may be re-presented up to 2 times within 180 days.

R10.name: Customer Advises Originator Not Known / Not Authorized
R10.note: The account holder says they never authorized the debit: possible fraud or account takeover.

R11.name: Customer Advises Entry Not in Accordance with Authorization
R11.note: The customer authorized something, but not this (for example, the wrong amount or date).

R16.name: Account Frozen / Entry Returned per OFAC Instruction
R16.note: The receiving account is frozen. If OFAC-related, compliance must review.

R20.name: Non-Transaction Account
R20.note: The account type doesn't allow ACH debits. The customer must link a checking account.

R29.name: Corporate Customer Advises Not Authorized
R29.note: A business account holder says the debit was not authorized.
